reviews.one_line_contribution: A contamination experiment that manipulates writer identity rather than content: relabelled-failure items are planted in one fixed bank at a fixed rate by five writers placed on a measured policy-agreement axis, and the claim is that harm to a reader rises with writer-reader proximity (peaking on the reader's own failures, reversing when the reader is swapped) while read-time detectability falls on the same diagonal, so that a foreign-backbone judge filters harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified papers split the claim between them. (a) arXiv:2606.24428 (verified by id; 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning', 2026-06-23) already names self-confirmatory error in agentic experience construction as the problem and already prescribes the proposal's remedy - multiple heterogeneous agents verifying experience before it is stored - with reported gains over strong baselines. It does not, from its abstract, measure a proximity gradient, run a mirror reader, or score a judge x writer detection table, so it does not scoop P1/P2/P3; but it does mean the practical payload of P5 ('use a foreign model to filter the bank') is an existing recipe, not a discovery, which caps the significance of the proposal's most useful arm. (b) arXiv:2502.04313 (verified by id; 'Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight') makes the general form of the detection claim - similar models make correlated mistakes, so using another model for oversight is risky in proportion to similarity - which is exactly P3's mechanism one level up, with a similarity metric already in hand; the proposal's contribution against it is the agent-experience stimulus and the harm-side consequence, not the mechanism. Add the documented self-detection literature the proposal never cites: arXiv:2507.02778 (Self-Correction Bench: models fix identical errors attributed to an external source but not in their own output) and arXiv:2410.21819 (self-preference bias in LLM-as-a-judge tracks familiarity/perplexity, not quality). Against that background, P3 is a transposition of a known effect to a new stimulus. The verified arXiv:2607.10608 (Compliance Trap) is a weaker threat than the proposal fears: it varies the reader and not the writer and has no read-time detector, so the harm half (P1, P2) does remain unmeasured in the agent-memory literature I could verify.
reviews.strongest_objection: The proximity manipulation does not isolate proximity from item text, so the headline can be confirmed and still not mean what the title says. pi(Q-self) is 1.0 by construction (the writer is the reader's own collection policy, probed on the reader's own k=0 states), so the axis has its anchor at a definitional ceiling, and Q-self items are simultaneously the highest-likelihood, most stylistically self-similar text in the whole experiment. A simple imitation account - a reader copies the items its own decoder assigns high likelihood to, regardless of who wrote them - predicts the entire harm ordering, the mirror reversal, and the diagonal detection deficit, and the design never measures the mediator (per-item reader log-likelihood/perplexity, matched across writers). The two arms meant to break this tie make it worse: Q-prox-S disables thinking and swaps the ReAct template, which is a format change the proposal itself declares out of scope as a separate axis (thoughts_do_not_travel), and Q-prox-T raises temperature until pi drops 0.15, which degrades text coherence as well as agreement. So P2's 'proximity, not backbone' contrast is confounded with format and with item quality, and P1's proximity reading is confounded with self-likelihood. Second-order but real: P3 is near-entailed as the entailment check says - the 5 percent false-rejection point is calibrated only on Q's clean expert items, so ordinary self-text leniency (arXiv:2410.21819) produces a diagonal deficit arithmetically, and the judge-overall-recall covariate removes a main effect, not that leniency. Third: every margin rests on an extrapolated half-width (8 x sqrt(1/s1+1/s2)) applied to a +/-8 floor measured at 2 seeds; the game-level variance component does not shrink with seeds and the arms differ in bank content, so the claimed +/-3.3 at 12v12 is asserted rather than derived from a variance decomposition of Measurements A and C.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Measure and report the mediator: per-contaminant log-likelihood under reader Q, and add one writer cell that is far in backbone but matched to Q-self in reader-likelihood (or reweight the E-self pool to match the Q-self likelihood distribution). If harm tracks likelihood rather than pi, that is the real finding and the design should be able to say so. (2) Replace Q-prox-S: hold format fixed (thinking on, same template) and get the pi drop from a different sampling policy or a checkpoint/prompt perturbation, so P2 is not a format contrast; report item-text statistics (length, thought-token share, invalid-command rate) per writer, since 'stylistic distance is equal across writers' is currently asserted, not measured. (3) Calibrate each judge's operating point per writer column on that writer's own clean successes (collect clean items for E and G, not only Q), or subtract the clean-item self-preference gap from each deficit, so P3 measures failure detection rather than familiarity. (4) Add the authorship-attribution control the self-correction literature demands: the same masked items shown to judge Q labelled as its own versus as another agent's - this separates text familiarity from attribution at near-zero cost and is what makes the result a 'blind spot' rather than a perplexity effect. (5) Raise the mirror reader to 12 seeds or state its result as descriptive; at 6 seeds with an unknown reader-E clean gain the arm that separates proximity from a writer property is the weakest cell in the design. (6) Add one contamination rate below 0.5 (0.1 or 0.2, the realistic regime for a success-filtered shared store) to the confirmatory plan instead of only the optional rate-1.0 slope. (7) Publish the game-versus-seed variance decomposition from Measurement A/C before pre-registering the +/-3.3 margins.
reviews.missing_baseline: A decorrelated same-backbone judge. The plan uses Q-prox variants as writers but never as judges, so 'foreign judge' is always a different backbone, and P5's conclusion ('writer identity is a required field; you need a second model') is untested against the cheapest thing a practitioner would try first: Q itself at a different temperature, a different scaffold, an ensemble of self-consistency samples, or Q asked about the item framed as a third party's trajectory. If a re-scaffolded or ensembled Q recovers most of the harm that the own-judgment filter misses, the foreign-backbone story collapses to 'any decorrelated judge', and P3's diagonal becomes a prompting artifact rather than a backbone property. Adding this judge column costs no new episodes - it reuses the same 600 items at the same operating point. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also name: a reader-likelihood/perplexity ranking filter as a model-free detector (the terminal-line regex is a straw detector, recall 0 at L0 by construction), and a low contamination rate.

Three unverifiable ids out of nine in a Related Work whose job is to establish that nobody has done this is a weakness in itself. Judgment of the proposal's own check: it is above average for this pipeline - it names its channel, its queries, its retries and its ids, and it verified its closest named method by id, which most submissions do not. But it searched the wrong home vocabulary. It went to pseudo-label confirmation bias and missed the literature that actually owns its mechanism: the self-correction blind spot (2507.02778, and the 2026 formal account 2607.09803 that its own novelty card surfaced at the top and it does not discuss), self-preference in LLM judges (2410.21819, 2608.18091), and model-similarity-limits-oversight (2502.04313). It also missed 2606.24428, a June 2026 preprint that is the nearest recent work to its cross-judge remedy in exactly its setting. Novelty is therefore scored on what survives: the harm half (P1/P2 - proximity-graded harm with a mirror reader and a manufactured, non-adversarial contaminant) is unmeasured in what I verified; the detection half (P3/P4) and the filter (P5) are transpositions of documented effects and an existing recipe.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That contamination in a shared experience bank is governed by writer-reader policy proximity rather than by writer capability or item content: relabelled failures written by the reader's own policy both harm the reader most and are the items the reader's own read-time judgment is least able to reject, with a foreign-backbone judge recovering the harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified: arXiv:2606.24428, 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning' (2026-06-23, S2, 1 citation) — it already names the self-confirmation trap in agentic experience learning and already fixes it with multiple *heterogeneous* agents verifying experiences before they enter the store. That is the proposal's P5 mechanism (a foreign judge filters what the writer's own judgment endorses), demonstrated end-to-end and shown to beat baselines. It does not manipulate writer identity as an independent variable, does not report per-writer detection precision/recall in a judge x writer table, and does not measure downstream harm as a function of measured policy proximity, so it does not scoop the interaction claim; but it does mean the proposal's practical payload ('use a different backbone to filter the bank') is already published advice, and a reviewer will read P5 as confirmation rather than discovery. Second threat, and the one the proposal never cites: the self-correction blind spot line — arXiv:2507.02778 Self-Correction Bench (verified, 16 citations: LLMs reliably fix an identical error attributed to an external source and fail to fix it in their own output, established by controlled error injection) and arXiv:2607.09803 (verified, 2026-07-09, a formal account of the same effect). P3 and P4 are that phenomenon re-measured on ALFWorld trajectories; the proposal's contribution there is the agentic instantiation, not the effect. Third: arXiv:2410.21819 Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge (verified, 286 citations) shows judge leniency tracks familiarity/perplexity of the text, and arXiv:2608.18091 (verified) shows authorship labels alone drive bidirectional judge bias — these are not just prior work, they are the confound in P3 (see strongest objection). The Compliance Trap arXiv:2607.10608 (verified) and MemoryGraft arXiv:2512.16962 (verified, 59 citations) are correctly positioned and do not threaten the claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: The detection half of the title ('least able to detect') is confounded with ordinary self-preference, and the design as written cannot separate them. Each judge's operating point is calibrated to a 5 percent false-rejection rate on *clean expert items only* — a single, writer-agnostic threshold — and the diagonal deficit is then read off recall in the judge x writer table. But a judge that is uniformly more lenient toward its own backbone's prose (documented, familiarity/perplexity-driven, 2410.21819; authorship-label-driven, 2608.18091) produces exactly a diagonal recall deficit at a threshold calibrated on someone else's text, with no failure-detection blind spot required. The pre-registered covariate (each judge's overall recall) removes a judge main effect, not self-text leniency, so it does not fix this. The proposal collects 600 clean self items for Q only, so it cannot even estimate the per-column self-preference offset for E or G. P4 is offered as the rescue, but the entailment check is right that its L1 falsifier is nearly unreachable (it demands CI upper bounds below 0.05 for *both* judges against a ~0.063 paired half-width, i.e. point estimates below -0.013 twice over), so the arm that is supposed to show the deficit is about judging actions rather than trusting an appended label will in practice return 'underpowered' rather than adjudicate. Second blade: the one arm that converts P1 from 'Q's failed text hurts Q' into a proximity claim — the reader-E mirror, D_E — is the least powered cell in the design (6 vs 6 seeds, half-width 4.6) and sits on a reader whose clean gain is itself unmeasured and may be small. If D_E lands inconclusive, the headline reduces to a single-reader observation compatible with 'Q-self failures are simply worse text', and the proposal's own risk section concedes the mirror is a sign test, not a margin test.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Calibrate the 5 percent false-rejection point per judge *per writer column* on that writer's own clean successes — which requires collecting clean success items for E and G, not only Q — or subtract the measured clean-item self-preference gap from each deficit and pre-register the adjusted deficit as the estimand. Without this the deficit measures style familiarity and P3 is near-entailed. (2) Restate P4's L1 clause as a single-deficit inferiority test (CI excluding 0.08, or the L0-minus-L1 drop CI excluding zero) and raise per-writer item counts from 600 toward 2,000; item-level judgments are cheap relative to the 28k episodes. (3) Run the filter cells on the E-self bank as well as the Q-self bank (Q-filters-E and E-filters-E), so P5 tests the diagonal at the harm level instead of comparing two judges on one bank; add a removal-rate-matched random-deletion control so 'foreign filter is better' cannot be 'foreign filter removed more items'. (4) Express R(cross) as a fraction of realised harm(Q-self) rather than a fixed 6 net, since at the Gate-0 floor of 6 the stated margin demands near-total recovery. (5) Raise the reader-E mirror to at least 8 seeds and pre-register a minimum clean gain for reader E, since the mirror is what makes this a proximity paper. (6) Cite and position against the self-correction blind spot literature explicitly — a reviewer who knows 2507.02778 will otherwise read P3/P4 as a port.
reviews.missing_baseline: Filter cells on the foreign writer's bank. P5 runs own-judgment vs cross-judge filters on the Q-self bank only, so 'the foreign judge recovers harm the own judge cannot' is indistinguishable from 'EXAONE is simply a better trajectory judge on this item distribution' — the covariate adjustment that guards against this in the offline recall table has no counterpart in the downstream harm cells. The discriminating arms are Q-filters-the-E-self-bank and E-filters-the-E-self-bank at the same matched false-rejection point: proximity predicts a crossover, better-judge predicts E wins in both banks. Two 8-seed cells (~4,400 episodes) buy the entire causal claim of P5 and are omitted. Secondary omission: a removal-rate-matched random-deletion filter, without which any filter advantage is partly a bank-size effect.

ID verification, all via s2cli paper: VERIFIED 2512.16962, 2607.10608, 2605.23723, 2606.30566, 2603.02240, 2602.00428, 2605.22842, 2310.14814, 2403.03095 (note: it is 'Cross Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Audio-Visual Source Localization', an odd anchor for the cross-judge analogy), 2606.24428, 2507.02778, 2607.09803, 2410.21819, 2608.18091. COULD NOT VERIFY: arXiv:2608.10509, cited in Related Work as 'provenance gating' — not found on S2 or HF; the proposal should drop or correct it. Judgment on the proposal's check: it names its channel, its queries, its retry strategy and its IDs, and it verifies its closest named result by ID, which is what the round asks for. But its 'home vocabulary' search went to semi-supervised pseudo-labeling, a distant analogy, and therefore missed the actual home literature of its own mechanism — the LLM self-correction blind spot, where the effect it predicts in P3/P4 has already been established by controlled error injection (2507.02778), and LLM-judge self-preference, which is simultaneously the nearest prior result and the confound in its measurement (2410.21819, 2608.18091). It also missed 2606.24428, published two months before the check was run, which names the self-confirmation trap in agentic experience learning and already deploys the heterogeneous-verifier remedy that P5 proposes to discover. None of these manipulates writer identity in a shared experience bank, measures per-writer downstream harm, or supplies the reader-swap reversal, so novelty is not capped — but it is reduced from 'new mechanism' to 'new interaction of two documented mechanisms', and the check as submitted overstates how clear the field is.

reviews.one_line_contribution: The first controlled measurement of contamination harm in an agent experience bank as a function of writer-reader policy proximity (own policy > same-backbone variant > foreign backbone), paired with a judge x writer detection table claiming a model is least able to flag masked failures written by its own backbone and that a foreign judge's filter recovers harm the reader's own judgment cannot.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified threat: arXiv:2606.24428 'Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning' (2026-06-23, s2, 1 citation, verified via s2cli paper) already frames self-written experience as a self-confirmation problem and already prescribes the proposal's remedy - heterogeneous (foreign) agents verifying experience before it enters the bank - as a working method. It does not, as far as its abstract goes, manipulate writer identity at fixed content, measure harm-versus-proximity, or produce a judge x writer recall table, so P1/P2 survive; but P5's 'a foreign judge's filter beats the reader's own' is close to a published recipe, and an AC will read the proposal as measuring why EDV works rather than as a new claim. Second threat, verified: the detection half is a transplant of an established effect. arXiv:2404.13076 'LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations', arXiv:2410.21819 'Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge' (bias tracks familiarity/perplexity of the text, which is exactly the proposal's mechanism), arXiv:2507.02778 'Self-Correction Bench: the Self-Correction Blind Spot', arXiv:2607.09803 (a formal/spectral model of that blind spot), arXiv:2608.18091 (self- vs other-labels induce bidirectional judge bias) and arXiv:2512.02304 'When Does Verification Pay Off?' (solver-verifier systems work better across model families) together predict P3, P4 and the offline half of P5 before any experiment is run. Not one of these appears in the proposal's Related Work or its collision check, even though its own title word is 'blind spot'. Also close, same environment: arXiv:2605.29463 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (2026-05, verified) shows on ALFWorld that self-generated reflective memory stores confident false task interpretations that persist across resets, and that replacing self-diagnosis with programmatic extraction fixes it - the harm-from-your-own-memory claim in the proposal's own environment, without the writer-identity manipulation. Note on the proposal's own citations: I verified 2512.16962, 2607.10608, 2605.23723, 2603.02240, 2608.10509, 2602.00428, 2605.22842, 2310.14814 and 2403.03095 by id; arXiv:2606.30566 ('forensic trajectory signatures'), cited in Related Work, does NOT resolve on either channel and I could not verify it exists.
reviews.strongest_objection: The contaminant sets are matched on type, length and a coarse coherence filter, but not on how wrong the failure is - and that, not writer proximity, is the likeliest driver of the harm ordering. Each writer's failure pool is conditioned on that writer's own success rate: Q-self fails on 47% of its training games and contributes many near-misses (correct procedure, wrong final receptacle); gpt-oss-120b 'fails rarely' and therefore contributes only catastrophic failures; EXAONE sits somewhere between. Type-matching within pick/heat/cool does not equalise the residual procedure correctness of the trajectory, and a masked near-miss and a masked disaster are different contaminants regardless of who wrote them. Worse for the headline, the two are anti-correlated with proximity in a way that can produce D_Q >= 5 with no proximity mechanism at all: the closest writer supplies the most plausible-looking, most executable, most nearly-correct wrong procedures, which is a content property that would survive a change of author. The proposal's separation of proximity from backbone (Q-prox-T/S) does not touch this, because raising temperature or swapping the ReAct template also changes what the failures look like; the manipulation check only gates pi and k=0 success, not failure quality. There is no arm in which the same failed action sequence is re-authored by a different writer, so 'written by my policy' is never separated from 'the actions my policy would have produced' or from 'this failure was closer to correct'. A reviewer will say the design measures a property of each writer's failure distribution and labels it proximity. The second-order version of the same objection: the confirmatory margins are arithmetically hard because they are bounded by total harm - D_Q >= 5 net requires E-self to be nearly harmless if Gate 0 lands near its 6-net floor, and R(cross) >= 6 net requires near-complete removal at that same floor (the entailment check flags this) - so the modal outcome of this expensive plan is a page of intervals reported as underpowered.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a re-authoring cross-over arm: take Q-self's masked failed trajectories and have E re-emit them in its own voice with the action content held fixed, and vice versa (verified by action-sequence equality, only surface form allowed to change), then run both. Harm that follows the actions rather than the author kills the proximity account cleanly; harm that follows the author is the paper. This is the arm that turns a correlational writer contrast into the claimed mechanism, and it is cheap relative to the 28,496 episodes already planned. (2) Match contaminants across writers on a measured wrongness score - fraction of the reference walkthrough achieved, or first divergent step - and report harm within wrongness stratum, not only within type and length. (3) Calibrate each judge's 5% false-rejection operating point per writer column on that writer's clean successes (collect clean items for every writer, not only for Q), and report the diagonal deficit net of the clean-item self-preference gap; as written, the operating point is set on clean expert items only, so the deficit measures style familiarity - the already-published self-preference effect - as much as failure blindness. (4) Run the mirror filter cells (own vs cross judge on the E-self bank) so P5 is not a statement that E is simply the better judge. (5) Express P5's recovery as a fraction of realised harm(Q-self), as rho_c already is, instead of a fixed 6 net. (6) Rewrite Related Work against the self-preference / self-correction-blind-spot literature and against 2606.24428, and state what the proposal adds beyond them - most defensibly: proximity as a graded axis, and the harm side, which none of them measures. (7) Drop or demote P4: at a paired half-width of ~0.063 its stated falsifier requires a negative point estimate in both judges at once, so it cannot fail in practice at 600 items per writer.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First, the symmetric filter arm: the own-judgment vs cross-judge filter cells are run only on the Q-self bank, so 'the foreign judge's filter recovers more' is confounded with 'E is a better judge of everything'. The interaction covariate protects the offline detection table but not the two downstream filter cells that P5 actually rests on; the missing cells are filter-by-Q and filter-by-E applied to the E-self bank (reader Q), which is the only way the foreignness of the judge is separated from its quality. Second, and cheaper than any judge: a provenance-only filter that drops every self-written item without reading it. The proposal's stated payoff is that 'writer identity, not just content, is a required field for any read-time filter' - the baseline for that claim is filtering on the field alone, which costs zero inference and, if the headline P1 is true, removes exactly the worst contaminants. If the foreign-judge filter does not beat the provenance filter, the detection half of the paper has no practical consequence. (A third, minor: the terminal-line regex is reported for scale, but no length- or perplexity-based cheap detector is run, and the self-preference literature says perplexity is the operative variable.)
